changes.historical_text: Select 1 monster on your opponent's side of the field and equip it to this card (this effect can only be used once per turn and you can only equip 1 monster at a time to this card). The ATK and DEF of this card become the same amounts as the monster equipped to this card. If this card is destroyed as a result of battle, the equipped monster is destroyed instead, and any battle damage you received from the battle is also inflicted to your opponent's Life Points.
changes.summary: Period behaviour on equipped Trap Monsters: the modern ATK and DEF value functions return 0 when the equipped card's original type is not a monster (g:GetFirst():GetOriginalType()&TYPE_MONSTER==0), so equipping a Trap Monster leaves Relinquished at 0/0; the GOAT variant omits that test and copies the equipped Trap Monster's printed ATK/DEF, keeping only the face-down and negative-value guards (upstream annotation: 'Gains stats of trap monsters as well'). Chronology unresolved: nothing in the packet dates when the original-type test was introduced.

review.notes: Baseline implements lineage v2 (DB1-EN015, Dark Beginning 1, 2004-10-12) exactly, so the chain starts there. v0/v1 (both MRL-029, Spell Ruler, 2002-09-16; the pair differs only by 'Magic' -> 'Spell') describe a much narrower replacement - 'When your opponent's monster attacks this monster with an ATK higher than Relinquished' - and predate the baseline, so they are recorded here rather than as changes. v2 -> v5 (LED2-EN000, 2018-02-22) is wording modernisation: select -> target, '(max. 1)' for the equip limit, the ritual-spell listing 'You can Ritual Summon this card with "Black Illusion Ritual"' added at v4 (LCYW-EN113, 2012-09-29), and the damage clause restated as 'While equipped with that monster, any battle damage you take from battles involving this card inflicts equal effect damage to your opponent'. That last one looks like it could be behavioural (v2 phrases the reflection as part of the destruction-replacement sentence) but is not: both scripts apply the reflection as a standing effect for any battle involving this card while a monster is equipped, and both keep the once-per-turn equip and the EFFECT_DESTROY_SUBSTITUTE replacement unchanged. Remaining diff lines are idiom: e1 -> e2 rename, RESET_EVENT| vs +, the s.listed_names metadata table, and Duel.GetAttacker()/Duel.GetAttackTarget() vs c:IsRelateToBattle() as equivalent formulations of 'this card was in the battle' (no period claim is made from that line).
